title: Capacity snapshot + what-if burst UX notes
content:
Quick context
- Goal: prototype a compact, operational UI that lets SREs and platform owners understand current pool state (snapshots), run what-if simulations for bursts, and perform batch edits to reservations.
- Motivation: operators keep hopping between metrics, raw quota tables, and the reservation timeline. Need a single surface for rapid triage + planning.
- Audience: infra ops, solutions engineers, and engineering PMs who manage Dedicated capacity.

High-level UX principles
- Single-pane summary + progressive disclosure (keep critical controls visible, hide heavy config behind an "Advanced" drawer).
- Lightweight simulation: non-destructive, preview-only by default, with clear commit step and audit trail.
- Batch-first: allow CSV or multi-select edits to reservations (common ask from SEs onboarding customers).
- Predictive heuristics: show suggested burst sizes and likely latency impact (back-of-envelope) so teams don't oversubscribe.

Feature sketches / wireframe notes
1) Capacity Snapshot card (top-left)
- Compact header: pool name, region, GPU type, reserved commit %, live-utilization (5m average).
- Mini heat/histogram: recent 24h tokenized usage (bars) with overlay line for avg latency. Hover shows exact numbers.
- Simple controls: dropdown to switch to 'last 1h / 6h / 24h / 7d' windows.
- Action buttons: "Open reservation editor" | "Run what-if" | "Export CSV"

2) Reservation list (center pane)
- Table columns: reservation id (short), owner/team, start-end, capacity (vGPU units), priority (chip), linked app, status (active/pending/expired), note icon.
- Inline batch-select checkboxes -> top bar shows aggregate selected capacity and a small CTA: "Reduce by 10% / Move to another pool / Cancel"
- Lightweight inline edit: click capacity cell to open small +/- control or paste numeric. Hitting Enter changes preview only (yellow underline).
- Undo stack visible: shows last changes in this session (stack count).

3) Batch Reservation Editor (drawer)
- CSV import area: accepts reservation id OR owner+dates to match existing rows. Minimal parsing rules shown.
- Operations: bulk-shift-dates, capacity-scale (percent), change priority tag, map to different pool.
- Preview diff table: left=existing, right=proposed, color-coded (green downscales, red upscales).
- Commit modal: summarize net capacity delta by pool, expected cost delta, link to billing calc.

4) What-if Burst Simulator (right pane, resizable)
- Input controls: desired burst start, duration slider (15m increments), target capacity delta (absolute or %), confidence slider (low/med/high) that toggles heuristics for headroom.
- Visual: time-based occupancy chart with dashed line showing simulated utilization. Overlay a small gray band showing expected scheduling delay (ms) under that load (computed from simple model).
- Recommendations: if burst > safe threshold, show suggested fallback: autobalance to another region, or fall back to smaller model variant.
- Safety checks: red badge if simulation violates SLA target (p95 latency > configured SLO).

5) Soft-priority matrix (new idea)
- 2D grid: vertical = team priority (low->high), horizontal = request flexibility (strict time windows -> flexible). Each reservation card lives in a cell; drag & drop to propose priority changes.
- Upon DnD: show a soft-impact preview (e.g., this move will evict X capacity during 3-4pm window).

6) Temporal heatmap + reservation stacking view (bottom)
- Heatmap showing pool saturation by 15m buckets for next 7 days. Reservation bars stack when overlapping; hover reveals reservation meta.
- Quick filter chips: show only customer-visible reservations, internal test jobs, scheduled maintenance.

Operational concerns / edge cases
- Race conditions: multiple operators editing same reservation set -> require optimistic locking and clear conflict resolution. Show "Your changes conflict with recent commit by {name}. Merge?"
- Audits: every committed what-if must create an audit entry with before/after snapshot + user comment. Add default comment template.
- Partial match in CSV import: warn and show rows that couldn't be matched. Provide ability to create new reservations from unmatched CSV rows.
- Billing calc: simulation should use current pricing and show estimated incremental cost. Add link to dedicated billing page for final invoice estimation.

Accessibility / performance notes
- Avoid giant JS tables; virtualize rows. Keep top-level metrics server-rendered to load fast.
- Keyboard support for table edits and batch operations.
- Color palette: use patterns/labels not just color to indicate state (for colorblind users).

Open questions to resolve in grooming
- Heuristics for latency estimation: ask APPLIED-ML for a simple model or use a conservative multiplier. (Linked: JIRA-INF-2145)
- Where should the cost calc live? Frontend approximation vs server-side accurate estimate? (tradeoffs: speed vs accuracy)
- Should what-if simulations reserve ephemeral capacity to guarantee simulation fidelity (i.e., create a soft reservation) or always be read-only previews?

Backlog slices (suggested tickets)
- WIRE-101: capacity snapshot component + API contract (fields needed)
- WIRE-102: reservation table with inline edits + undo stack
- WIRE-103: CSV import + batch editor (parsing rules doc)
- WIRE-104: what-if simulator MVP (UI + simple latency model)
- WIRE-105: soft-priority matrix prototype (drag/drop)
- WIRE-106: audit trail + commit modal + comment template

Quick implementation notes for engineers
- API: snapshot endpoint should return: pool_meta, 24h_usage_histogram (15m buckets), reservation_summary (ids + lightweight metadata). Keep reservation detail separate (lazy load) to speed up initial page.
- Use a shared visualization lib for heatmap and histogram (reuse observability charts).
- CSV matching: prefer exact reservation id; fallback to owner+start_end fuzzy parse. Provide daily TTL on import matches to prevent stale edits.
- Feature flag: behind ff-team.capacity_snapshot_v1 for safe rollout.

Prototype tasks (design + PM)
- Quick Figma frames: top-level snapshot + right-sim panel + bottom heatmap. (Maya to produce by 2025-11-20)
- Usability check with 3 SREs (internal): run through common flows (scale-down, schedule burst, import CSV). Capture 5 pain points.

Notes from brainstorm session (raw)
- "Would be awesome to just drag time blocks on the heatmap to create a reservation" -> map to WIRE-103
- "Show me predicted throttling probability as a percent rather than raw ms" -> consider adding percentile indicator in simulator
- "We get a lot of one-off test reservations; allow tagging as ephemeral/test and auto-evict after 48h" -> small feature, high ops ROI

Next steps
- Lock down API fields with infra owners (action: Ethan to sync with infra team, target 2025-11-25)
- Design first-pass Figma mockups (Maya) + review 2025-11-27
- Create the initial ticket set and sizing (PM + eng)

-- end of notes --
